The second option, "Increases fat oxidation enough to improve high-intensity performance," is the closer fit, because low-carbohydrate intake does shift fuel use toward fat. However, its performance claim is doubtful, since high-intensity work depends on glycogen and low-carb diets usually impair it. The first option gets the direction wrong, because low carbohydrate intake reduces reliance on muscle glycogen rather than increasing it.

CONFIDENCE: 40
